children.approach: Dominated-twin lemma: if x != z in a left cell Gamma with D(z) subset D(x) and mu(y,z) >= mu(y,x) for every y in Gamma with D(y) not subset D(x), then v = c_z - c_x satisfies (1+s)v in cone(C_KL u {v}) for all s, and cone{c_w (w != z), v} is simplicial, invariant, strictly contains C_KL => C_KL not maximal. Sketch: s in D(z) => s in D(x): both killed; s in D(x)\D(z): (1+s)v = (1+s)c_z in C_KL; s not in D(x): (1+s)v = 2v + sum_{y: s in D(y)} (mu(y,z) - mu(y,x)) c_y, coefficients >= 0 since such y have D(y) not subset D(x). Basis change replaces c_z by c_z - c_x => simplicial.
children.notes: PROVE 279: written sober (Lemma A). Needs only mu>=0 (Elias-Williamson) and the GW convention-C action.

children.approach: B3 irreducible 3-dim left cell {x = s3s1, y = s2s3s1, z = s1s2s3s1}: D(x) = {1,3}, D(y) = {2}, D(z) = {1}; edges x-y, y-z; mu(x,z) = 0 (even length difference). v = c_z - c_x: (1+s1)v = 0, (1+s2)v = 2v, (1+s3)v = 2c_z. cone{c_x, c_y, v} invariant simplicial, strictly contains C_KL; module irreducible so the maximal cone C^max is unique (Mejstrik-Protasov) and strictly contains C_KL.
